text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- French President Jacques Chirac says his European policies are in unison with Bonn.
- Iranian police prevent protesters from storming German embassy in Tehran.
- Members of ruling coalition welcome compromise on pensions policy.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel insists Germany's budget deficit in 1997 will be 2.9 percent of GDP.
- Association of Young Businesspeople (BJU) survey reveals optimism that German economic performance will improve.
HANDELSBLATT
- Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt says Germany will make further savings if necessary to meet the criteria for European monetary union (EMU).
- BHW shares will cost between 22 and 28 deutschemarks.
- Plans to merge public broadcasters South German Broadcasting (SDR) and Southwest Broadcasting (SWF) complete.
- Liberal Free Democrats (FDP) divided over reaction to pensions compromise.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Tobacco retailers agree not to place cigarette machines near schools or youth centres.
- Spanish police search for two Germans suspected of aiding ETA guerrilla group.
- Confederation of German Industry (BDI) says Germany has lost ground as an industrial location.
- Iranian trade delegation still plans to visit Germany next week.
DIE WELT
- Both government and oppostion emphasise their stances on tax reform ahead of top-level meeting.
- Three of five "wise men" economic advisers predict Germany will not meet EMU criteria.
- BDI president Hans-Olaf Henkel says Germany now just "average" as an industrial location.
- German Chambers of Trade and Industry accuse Federal Labour Office of unnecessary panic over state of apprenticeship market.
